claims.claim: On 2026-10-15 arXiv authors introduced Harness-Delta Attribution
an evaluation protocol that splits an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and a remainder that upper-bounds residual generalizable improvement
They applied it to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks
In the 21 settings with statistically significant search-set gains, overfitting and test-time scaling accounted for 54% and 14% of the gain on average
with the combined share exceeding 50% in 14 settings
Search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks
the authors report that validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting
The residual is an upper bound
On 2026-10-11 arXiv authors introduced a scalable, fully automatic approach to weak-to-strong verifier hardening for agent environments
It first sets up an isolated verifier sandbox that agents cannot directly modify, then runs a hacker-fixer loop to find and repair remaining verifier vulnerabilities
Applied to Terminal Bench, KernelBench and SETA, it substantially reduced attack success
the iterative design produced progressively stronger defenses as loop iterations increased, outperforming the static, non-iterative baseline
An earlier version of the loop was adopted by the official Terminal Bench repository to audit exploits in its environments
